notes.meaning: A person dining with an important ruler needs to watch himself closely and pay attention to what is happening around him. The rich food and the honor of being invited can make someone forget how dangerous it is to displease a powerful host. A wise guest stays on guard instead of being dazzled by the courtly banquet.

Putting a knife to one's throat is a vivid picture of strictly controlling your appetite. Anyone who loves rich food must hold back by force rather than eat greedily in royal company. Failing to control personal desire before a powerful man can cost someone his reputation or even his life.

A guest should not long for a ruler's fine dishes, because such royal food is often deceitful. Leaders often hold grand banquets for their own political purposes rather than true friendship, hoping guests will let down their guard. Craving luxury can trap a person into making unwise promises or giving away secrets.

Do not exhaust your life trying to pile up earthly wealth, and stop relying on worldly cleverness to get ahead. Working moderately to care for family needs is good, but turning money into your life's goal brings endless toil and worry. True wisdom knows when to step back and be content with what God provides.

Riches are temporary and can vanish the moment someone sets his heart on them. Wealth behaves like a wild bird that suddenly grows strong wings and flies far away into the open sky. Putting ultimate trust in material things will only end in heartbreak when they suddenly disappear.

The writer warns against accepting a dinner invitation from a stingy or selfish person. A host with an evil eye desires everything for himself and hates the thought of parting with his food. Eating his fine meals will bring no real pleasure because he is not genuinely generous.

A selfish host may politely say eat and drink, but in his mind he is secretly calculating the cost of every bite. A person's real character is found in what he thinks inwardly, not in the polite compliments on his lips. His warm words are completely false, so his heart is not truly with his guest.

Discovering that a host resented the food makes the entire meal feel repulsive and sickening. Any kind compliments or words of gratitude spoken to him turn out to be entirely wasted. Accepting a grudging invitation leaves the guest feeling deeply uncomfortable and full of regret.

Do not waste good advice or holy teachings on an obstinate fool. Someone who rejects wisdom will only mock and look down on sound counsel instead of learning from it. In such moments, staying quiet is far better than throwing precious instruction away on someone who refuses to hear.

Never steal property by moving old boundary markers, and never take over farmland that belongs to defenseless orphans. Even if poor children have no family member left on earth to defend them, God Himself is their mighty Redeemer. The Lord will act as their nearest kin, taking them into His care and punishing anyone who oppresses them.

A student must actively direct his inner affections toward godly discipline and open his ears to wise teaching. Learning wisdom requires deliberate effort, honest listening, and a willingness to be corrected. God's truth must be welcomed deeply into the heart to reshape how one lives.

Parents are urged not to hold back necessary discipline from their growing children out of a fear of hurting them. Loving correction with a rod will not cause lasting bodily harm, but it helps rescue a child from foolish patterns that lead to early destruction. Wise guidance and faithful discipline protect a child's soul from the grave and from eternal ruin.

differ.view: Some charismatic teachers understand the rod as a symbol of loving parental correction and guidance rather than an absolute rule requiring physical punishment.
Some evangelicals teach that while physical discipline is permitted, parents should tailor correction to the child's temperament and avoid any harsh treatment.

notes.meaning: A godly parent experiences great joy when a son takes wisdom to heart and chooses what is right. Hearing honest, righteous words come from a child's mouth brings gladness to the parent's deepest feelings. Seeing children grow in godliness is the sweetest reward for all the labor and prayer spent on them.

Do not look with envy at the temporary success or freedom of wicked people, but remain devoted to the fear of the Lord throughout each day. The good fortune of sinners will soon end, while those who trust God have a sure future ahead of them. Faithful believers will never have their hope disappointed in the end.

The teacher urges the student to listen carefully, embrace wisdom, and deliberately keep his heart on God's straight path. The course of a person's life depends on what rules his heart, so inner desires must be guided with care. Walking in God's ways keeps a person from stumbling into dangerous side roads.

Stay away from the company of people who overindulge in heavy drinking and greedy feasting. Consuming excessive food and wine wastes resources, ruins health, and produces a constant state of lazy drowsiness. In time, such uncontrolled living strips a person of his livelihood and leaves him dressed in rags.

Children must honor and obey the father who brought them into the world, and they must never look down on their mother as she ages. Old age can leave parents frail and dependent, but it never takes away their rightful claim to respect and love. Caring for elderly parents is both a sacred duty and a mark of true wisdom.

A person must spare no effort or cost to gain God's truth, wisdom, discipline, and understanding. Once these precious gifts are acquired, they must never be traded away for earthly riches, popular approval, or easy pleasure. Living by God's truth is worth far more than anything this world can offer in return.

Parents feel deep gladness when their child grows up to be a righteous and sensible person. Knowing that a son walks in integrity makes all the pain and hard work of raising him feel well rewarded. Choosing the path of godly wisdom brings lasting honor and joy to the home.

God speaks through wisdom to ask for the complete devotion of the young person's heart and mind. The Lord wants our full affection and will not settle for a heart divided between Him and the world. Choosing to delight in His righteous ways protects a believer from wandering into deadly sins.

Sexual immorality is a dangerous trap, like a deep pit or a narrow well that is easy to fall into but almost impossible to climb out of. An immoral woman lies in wait like a bandit, ready to rob an unsuspecting person of his virtue, peace, and spiritual strength. Yielding to lust multiplies unfaithfulness in homes and brings widespread moral ruin.

The writer presents a riddle asking who constantly suffers from sorrow, bitter quarreling, needless injuries, and bloodshot eyes. The answer points directly to those who sit late drinking wine and constantly search out potent mixed liquors. Wasting hours on intoxicating drink creates endless misery and senseless physical harm.

Readers are told not to gaze with longing at wine when its bright red color sparkles in the cup and flows down easily. The drink looks attractive and enticing, but admiring it only fuels the desire to indulge without limit. Avoiding the attractive beginnings of temptation is the best defense against being overcome by sin.

While intoxicating drink may taste sweet at the start, its final result is deadly. In the end, alcohol strikes like a poisonous snake, leaving painful bites and venom in the body and mind. What promised pleasure ends in disease, broken lives, and the judgment of God.

Drunkenness inflames lustful passions, causing a person's eyes to look after immoral women. It also removes all moral filters from the heart and tongue, leading the drunkard to blurt out corrupt, foolish, and rebellious words. Losing control to alcohol quickly destroys personal dignity and leads to shameful behavior.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars translate the phrase as strange things rather than immoral women, viewing it as a reference to hallucinations and mental confusion caused by heavy drinking.

notes.meaning: An intoxicated person is compared to someone trying to sleep in the middle of a rough sea or perched on the top of a ship's rocking mast. He is in terrible and immediate danger of losing his life at any second. Yet because alcohol has dulled his senses, he feels completely secure and remains blind to the peril around him.

The drunken person wakes up groggy and battered from brawls, yet he is so numbed that he barely felt the blows. Instead of learning a lesson from his bruises and shame, his conscience is so hardened that his first desire upon waking is to chase after another drink. This picture exposes the terrible grip of addiction, which keeps driving a person back to the very habit that is destroying him.
